Which Meditation Is Right for Me?

The best meditation is the one you can sustain. Use this quick guide to choose a method that matches your current mind-state and lifestyle.

Japa (Mantra Repetition)

Best for: Busy, distracted minds that need a simple anchor

Typical time: 10–20 min

How to start: Repeat one mantra with breath for 108 counts

Learn this method

Dhyana (Silent Meditation)

Best for: Seekers drawn to stillness and witness awareness

Typical time: 15–30 min

How to start: Sit still and return attention to pure awareness

Learn this method

Pranayama-led Meditation

Best for: Anxious or restless nervous systems

Typical time: 8–15 min

How to start: Begin with breath regulation, then sit in quiet

Learn this method

Self-Inquiry

Best for: Philosophically inclined seekers

Typical time: 10–25 min

How to start: Ask “Who am I?” and trace attention to its source

Learn this method

Decision shortcut

If your mind is noisy: begin with Japa.

If your body is tense: begin with Pranayama.

If you love direct contemplation: begin with Self-Inquiry.
